note: Generic owner step for every writable bind volume, replacing the per-volume elasticsearch_data_init and wiki_static_init. A fresh directory under runtime/volumes/ belongs to the host user, so on a Linux or WSL2 host a non-root writer cannot use it unless the host uid happens to match (redis is uid 999, the others 1000). `compose render` fills `volumes` and `command` from the profile (compose.with_owner_init): each volume goes to the `user:` of the services that mount it writable, and those services wait with service_completed_successfully. Services that keep root and fix their own ownership (postgres, mongo, rabbitmq, unoconv; the `user` control in manifest/hardening.json) are left alone. It runs the elasticsearch2 image because that is the one locally built image every profile has. Explicit root (run_as 0:0) with cap_drop ALL and only CAP_CHOWN, read-only root, no-new-privileges, one hardening exception. On Docker Desktop for Mac chown is a no-op and the step changes nothing. Idempotent.
